CONSUMES a MODEL-CONTROLLED tool-call envelope on stdin: that input is untrusted and is parsed without shell evaluation, with each contracted field type-asserted rather than coerced (ADR-156, #7164 — an array tool_input.command previously reached eval AND evaded every anchored guard). Prior description said only what hooks DO, never what they CONSUME. A PreToolUse hook also has a THIRD disposition beyond allow/deny: it may REWRITE tool_input before execution and let the call proceed (ADR-162, #7165) — grep-rewrite.sh prepends a grep() redefinition that neutralizes the ugrep shim which reached 9.5 GB RSS against a 21 kB file, leaving the command byte-identical. Bounded by a SINGLE-REWRITER invariant: updatedInput REPLACES tool_input (it does not merge), a sibling deny still wins, and permission rules match the ORIGINAL command. Additionally, in the repo-local `.claude/` hook surface only — never the shipped plugin surface — it enforces host resource control: at SessionStart it adopts the agent process tree into a memory-capped systemd transient scope (ADR-161). Where this container runs server-side there is no per-user systemd bus, so that path declines and does nothing. TWO HARNESSES: `.claude/hooks/` (Claude Code) and three blocking PreToolUse mirrors in `.openhands/hooks/`, which consume a different envelope over a protocol with no `ask` state — so ADR-157's posture is split by reason class there (ADR-165). On the `.claude` side exit 0 is the precondition for that posture at all: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout JSON entirely (#7190). The two-harness enumeration describes where hook CODE lives; since ADR-178 (#7409) it no longer describes where its concurrency layer comes from — `lib/incidents.sh`, `lib/log-rotation.sh` and `pre-merge-rebase.sh` source the session-state lock/lease primitives from a THIRD, shipped location inside the deployed plugin root, reaching in from the repo side. External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. The read direction is unchanged and is still the ONLY thing that grades a CI-emitted marker: the emitter's exit code is not evidence, so a run is green only after it reads its own run_id back out through the ClickHouse path (ADR-172 §2). Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and the object pool may be at 10/10. git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). ALSO a per-host origin absence detector that probes each web host's CF-proxied hostname (web-N.app.soleur.ai/health) directly, so a dead/never-booted host pages with per-host attribution the round-robin monitors cannot give (#5933 Item 1). SINCE #7798/ADR-204 IT ALSO OWNS A PROPERTY SENTRY STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS: betteruptime_monitor.soleur_www_redirect ('soleur dot ai www redirect 301', uptime-alerts.tf) asserts that https://www.soleur.ai/ returns exactly 301 WITHOUT following it (follow_redirects = false, remember_cookies = false — the vendor rejects a 3xx expectation with either enabled, HTTP 422). Sentry's uptime checker always follows 3xx and grades the FINAL response, so its predecessor sentry_uptime_monitor.soleur_www asserted `equals 301` against the apex's 200 -- an assertion it CANNOT satisfy (structural; the measurement behind it is 10/10 most recent checks failing on 2026-09-07, not a paged-back 101-day census). That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage).

nodes.title: Cloudflare Tunnel

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

nodes.technology: cloudflared (ONE tunnel; ONE connector live in prod: web-1 — web-2 retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463). The web_tunnel_connector gate is construction-time only)

description.txt: Severity-ranked operational-notification store (ADR-085, #6007). Mutable read/act/archive state, workspace-grain, Owner-shared reads — SEPARATE from the email-triage WORM statutory ledger. Content-minimized (title + source_ref ids only). GET /api/inbox merges it with email-triage into one severity-ordered feed (statutory pinned first).

Owner-private beta-tester / prospect CRM (ADR-102, #6165). Third-party contact PII + dual-lens conversation notes + append-only stage-transition history. Owner-only RLS; writes RPC-only via auth.uid()-pinned SECURITY DEFINER functions; the cro/cpo agents read AND write via the crm_* MCP tools (agent-native parity). 24-month retention; Art. 17 via ON DELETE CASCADE + crm_erase_contact.

Self-hosted EU Redis — ADR-059 replay buffer + session/control state; network-reachable, per-workspace key namespacing, TLS + requirepass. DISTINCT node from the loopback Inngest Redis (ADR-068 Phase 4a). AT REST: unconfirmed from code alone — no session-store host posture probe exists in the code-sourced audit. Recorded as a ledgered exception rather than asserted (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897), pending a live pull of the host's actual state
Placement, health-reschedule, and rolling deploys across the Hetzner cluster (ADR-068 Phase 4a)

Co-located stateless sticky router (in each web-host process, not a separate box) — resolves a session's owning host from the per-user worktree lease at the WS-upgrade handshake; local ⇒ serve, remote ⇒ proxy over one-way-TLS private net. Control ops are host-local (no cross-host forwarding). Lease in Postgres (ADR-068 user-sticky amendment)

Cluster of Hetzner Cloud hosts (Nomad clients, spread placement) running web app + CLI engine containers. Per-user worktrees are host-local in the ADR-068 §1 sense (they do NOT live on the shared git-data host) but they are NOT on the root NVMe — they sit on a per-host ATTACHED BLOCK VOLUME, workspacesVolume below (#6588 corrected this description, which said 'host-local NVMe' and led readers to conclude there was no volume to encrypt). At first boot a fresh host pulls the web app image from GHCR and extracts its baked bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl via docker cp (ADR-080, #5921) — a path web-1 can never take: the load-bearing reason is lifecycle{ignore_changes=[user_data]}, which means cloud-init never re-runs, so the bake reaches no live host (ADR-119 §(e)). ADR-143 (adopting, #6459) governs the return of a second web host: because cx33 was unorderable at the ADR-143 decision (2026-07-26 probe; still unorderable in hel1-dc2 on 2026-08-06, though it returned in nbg1-dc3/fsn1-dc14), web-2 returns as a fresh cattle **cpx22** (2c/4g x86, ~€19.49/mo net) — sized to web-1's MEASURED usage (~1.5 GB peak RAM / 0.48 load15 over 30d, not its over-provisioned 8g shape; ADR-143 D1) — a health-monitored standby at serving-weight 0 (NOT in the ingress rotation) until ADR-068 Phase-3 GA, since the sole-copy workspace volume lives on web-1 and a request routed to web-2 pre-flip would hit an empty workspace. TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-07-26 (ADR-143 addendum, #6966), FORCED BY STOCK: the live probe that day (/v1/datacenters .server_types.available) found the ENTIRE cx line — cx23 as well as cx33 — and the ENTIRE cax ARM line orderable in 0 of 3 EU DCs, so the earlier 'cx23, in stock in hel1' claim recorded here is FALSE and is retired. cpx22 matches cx23 on cores and RAM exactly (2c/4g) and doubles local disk, so the D1 sizing rationale is unchanged — this was a price change (+€14.00/mo), not a resize. Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. The fleet remains single-host until web-2 is provisioned by the gated web-host-create dispatch

description.txt: Every user's checked-out repository. SOLE-COPY: refs/checkpoints/* is pushed by no refspec, session-sync.ts autocommits only knowledge-base/**, and signup-provisioned workspaces have no git remote at all — so ADR-068 §1's 'GitHub remains the durable rehydration source' does NOT hold here and there is no durable second copy anywhere (no upstream to rehydrate from). ENCRYPTED AT REST as of the 2026-07-23 cutover — the gap #6588/ADR-119 opened (PLAINTEXT ext4 while the published privacy policy claimed LUKS) is closed. HISTORY: an earlier 2026-07-20 cutover attempt (run 29782780158) landed /mnt/data on crypto_LUKS for ~27 minutes before its own dead-man timer silently remounted the retained plaintext volume over it (#6812) — do not cite that landing as the current state. The 2026-07-23 cutover is the one that certified: `workspaces-luks-verify` run **30040444418** reported `SOLEUR_WORKSPACES_READYZ ready=true writable=true populated=true workspace_count=8 expected=8` against `/dev/mapper/workspaces` — a mechanically measured verdict, not an assumed one (this distinction, per ADR-140, is the whole feature). web-2's instance was knowingly left plaintext (never served, empty) until its 2026-07-17 teardown (#6538/#6463). The fleet is single-host as of this writing, so no plaintext member remains — but that is a statement about the CURRENT fleet, NOT an invariant: the fresh web-2 (repinned cpx22, #6966) is born with its own per-host workspaces volume (hcloud_volume.workspaces, web-2 key) as RAW/empty PLAINTEXT, because the guest-side LUKS path for a FRESH host is the deferred #6931 work (ADR-141 D3) and the workspaces_luks attachment is web-1-bound and outside the birth fan-out (#6964). That member holds NO user data (sole copy is web-1's volume; web-2 is never routed pre-flip, dns.tf app record is web-1-only and the #6575 anti-pooling gate fail-closes), and it MUST NOT take serving weight while plaintext — re-evaluate at the ADR-068 Phase-3 GA flip

nodes.title: Shared git-data

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). NOT YET PROVISIONED (#6977): this element is DECLARED in IaC and the host has never existed — an authenticated `terraform state list` returns zero git-data members — so every behaviour described here is the TARGET state, not the live one. It remains unborn until the gated `git-data-host-create` dispatch runs. The birth-readiness interlock that held that route is RELEASED by #6982, which ships the off-host emitter (ADR-149 item 1): the host now emits boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal the birth job POLLS, and gc faults to Better Stack — so a green apply and a dark host are no longer indistinguishable. What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), shipped unfired because a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. CORRECTED 2026-08-03 (#7204): the route is NO LONGER unfired — it has been dispatched FOUR times (one dry-run success 2026-07-30, then three real-host failures) and has consumed three paid cpx22 hosts IN THE SEPARATE #7025 REHEARSAL TERRAFORM ROOT — which is why 'the host has never existed' above stays true: no rehearsal host is ever created at the hcloud_server.git_data address. The most recent, run 30649892865, died at `stage:luks_open` with mount(2) returning ESRCH: the birth `mkfs.ext4 -O quota,project` set the ext4 quota feature, whose mount forces `ext4_enable_quotas()` and a `quota_v2` module the 24.04 cloud image does not ship (linux-modules-extra absent). That is the CURRENT birth-blocking fact, fixed by #7204 (ADR-159) but NOT yet re-rehearsed — the evidence file is still absent, so the gate still refuses. The runbook banner is a FURTHER hold, not the only one. AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). Ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897), pending cutover

description.txt: DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.

OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Pulled from the PUBLIC upstream registry at boot, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The LIVE device is still plaintext ext4 until the guarded `registry-luks-recut` workflow_dispatch is fired; that vehicle shipped UNFIRED (#6929), so this is a code-declared posture, NOT a live-verified one. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.

description.txt: Inngest durable queue + run-state. AOF on the persistent volume survives a host re-provision — the armed-reminder durability fix (#5450). AT REST: STILL PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.inngest_redis`, `format = "ext4"` under `ignore_changes = [format]` — inngest-host.tf) — a seized/snapshot disk exposes the queue + run-state AOF, i.e. in-flight job payloads. Recorded as a ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6894). CORRECTED 2026-09-03 (#7695): the LUKS APPARATUS NOW EXISTS and this node previously said it did not — cloud-init-inngest.yml carries a five-arm blkid discriminator, inngest-luks-open.service reopens the mapper on every later boot, and the passphrase is minted at merge (inngest-redis-luks.tf). The apparatus is INERT: it cuts nothing by itself. The device becomes crypto_LUKS only when the gated `apply_target=inngest-volume-recut` dispatch destroys and recreates the volume raw, which two guards refuse unless the host is measured dark and the store measured empty. So the AT-REST claim above is unchanged and the ledger keeps its exception — what changed is that the mechanism is built rather than absent

PRIVATE GHCR registry (ghcr.io/jikig-ai/soleur-web-platform + soleur-inngest-bootstrap) — the ORIGINAL host pull source, now WRITE-ONLY: still dual-pushed by CI, but DEAD AS A FALLBACK since the Phase-5 retirement — the read PAT is revoked (GET api.github.com/user -> 401) and the minter is disabled (GHCR_MINTER_DISABLED=true; pull-token mint -> 403 DENIED), verified 2026-07-30 (#7071). It receives every image and can serve none TO HOSTS. Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2.

DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.

Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Google 8.8.8.8, queried via node:dns Resolver.setServers() by cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue's DNS-propagation gate (#6698). Used to confirm the DNS-only flip actually reached the public internet before the cert poll begins — Cloudflare's TTL for proxied records is fixed at 300 s, so a proxy-status flip takes ~5-10 min to propagate and a poll started before then is guaranteed-wasted public-TLS-outage window. `dig` is deliberately NOT used: it is not installed in the app image (the Dockerfile installs only ca-certificates, git, bubblewrap, socat, qpdf, jq), so shelling out would throw at runtime.

The operator's own per-user systemd manager, reached over the D-Bus socket at /run/user/<uid>/bus (SO_PEERCRED-authenticated, same uid only, no network). Owns the cgroup v2 hierarchy for the login session: the Hook Engine asks IT to create the memory-capped transient scope each agent session runs in, so systemd stays the SINGLE WRITER to that hierarchy and no component writes cgroup directories directly (ADR-161). Units are transient and self-clean when their last process exits, so nothing is provisioned and nothing persists across a reboot.

Guards tool calls (blocks commits to main, rm -rf, etc.) AND injects additive context — phase-surface hints (ADR-070) and declarative skill context_queries (ADR-086). CONSUMES a MODEL-CONTROLLED tool-call envelope on stdin: that input is untrusted and is parsed without shell evaluation, with each contracted field type-asserted rather than coerced (ADR-156, #7164 — an array tool_input.command previously reached eval AND evaded every anchored guard). Prior description said only what hooks DO, never what they CONSUME. A PreToolUse hook also has a THIRD disposition beyond allow/deny: it may REWRITE tool_input before execution and let the call proceed (ADR-162, #7165) — grep-rewrite.sh prepends a grep() redefinition that neutralizes the ugrep shim which reached 9.5 GB RSS against a 21 kB file, leaving the command byte-identical. Bounded by a SINGLE-REWRITER invariant: updatedInput REPLACES tool_input (it does not merge), a sibling deny still wins, and permission rules match the ORIGINAL command. Additionally, in the repo-local `.claude/` hook surface only — never the shipped plugin surface — it enforces host resource control: at SessionStart it adopts the agent process tree into a memory-capped systemd transient scope (ADR-161). Where this container runs server-side there is no per-user systemd bus, so that path declines and does nothing. TWO HARNESSES: `.claude/hooks/` (Claude Code) and three blocking PreToolUse mirrors in `.openhands/hooks/`, which consume a different envelope over a protocol with no `ask` state — so ADR-157's posture is split by reason class there (ADR-165). On the `.claude` side exit 0 is the precondition for that posture at all: a non-zero exit makes Claude Code discard the hook's stdout JSON entirely (#7190). The two-harness enumeration describes where hook CODE lives; since ADR-178 (#7409) it no longer describes where its concurrency layer comes from — `lib/incidents.sh`, `lib/log-rotation.sh` and `pre-merge-rebase.sh` source the session-state lock/lease primitives from a THIRD, shipped location inside the deployed plugin root, reaching in from the repo side. Its TELEMETRY has a namespace contract (ADR-205, #7853): an emitted rule_id carrying a section prefix (hr/wg/cq/rf/pdr/cm) CLAIMS membership in the AGENTS corpus and is orphan-checked against it; one carrying no prefix is hook telemetry and is outside the corpus by construction, which replaced nine hand-maintained exemption stanzas in rule-metrics-aggregate.sh. Under test the sink is redirected at the RUNNER CHOKEPOINT — both bunfig preloads, the vitest globalSetup, the test-helpers.sh prelude and the _git_fixture_env import — never at the call site, and never by teaching this container to detect tests, because a false positive there would darken real operator telemetry.

description.txt: Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2.

Cluster of Hetzner Cloud hosts (Nomad clients, spread placement) running web app + CLI engine containers. Per-user worktrees are host-local in the ADR-068 §1 sense (they do NOT live on the shared git-data host) but they are NOT on the root NVMe — they sit on a per-host ATTACHED BLOCK VOLUME, workspacesVolume below (#6588 corrected this description, which said 'host-local NVMe' and led readers to conclude there was no volume to encrypt). At first boot a fresh host pulls the web app image from GHCR and extracts its baked bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl via docker cp (ADR-080, #5921) — a path web-1 can never take: the load-bearing reason is lifecycle{ignore_changes=[user_data]}, which means cloud-init never re-runs, so the bake reaches no live host (ADR-119 §(e)). ADR-143 (adopting, #6459) governs the return of a second web host: because cx33 was unorderable at the ADR-143 decision (2026-07-26 probe; still unorderable in hel1-dc2 on 2026-08-06, though it returned in nbg1-dc3/fsn1-dc14), web-2 returns as a fresh cattle **cpx22** (2c/4g x86, ~€19.49/mo net) — sized to web-1's MEASURED usage (~1.5 GB peak RAM / 0.48 load15 over 30d, not its over-provisioned 8g shape; ADR-143 D1) — a health-monitored standby at serving-weight 0 (NOT in the ingress rotation) until ADR-068 Phase-3 GA, since the sole-copy workspace volume lives on web-1 and a request routed to web-2 pre-flip would hit an empty workspace. TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-07-26 (ADR-143 addendum, #6966), FORCED BY STOCK: the live probe that day (/v1/datacenters .server_types.available) found the ENTIRE cx line — cx23 as well as cx33 — and the ENTIRE cax ARM line orderable in 0 of 3 EU DCs, so the earlier 'cx23, in stock in hel1' claim recorded here is FALSE and is retired. cpx22 matches cx23 on cores and RAM exactly (2c/4g) and doubles local disk, so the D1 sizing rationale is unchanged — this was a price change (+€14.00/mo), not a resize. Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. The fleet remains single-host until web-2 is provisioned by the gated web-host-create dispatch

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

description.txt: OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Pulled from the PUBLIC upstream registry at boot, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The LIVE device is still plaintext ext4 until the guarded `registry-luks-recut` workflow_dispatch is fired; that vehicle shipped UNFIRED (#6929), so this is a code-declared posture, NOT a live-verified one. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.

description.txt: Centralized secrets management with runtime injection

External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. The read direction is unchanged and is still the ONLY thing that grades a CI-emitted marker: the emitter's exit code is not evidence, so a run is green only after it reads its own run_id back out through the ClickHouse path (ADR-172 §2). Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and the object pool may be at 10/10. git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). ALSO a per-host origin absence detector that probes each web host's CF-proxied hostname (web-N.app.soleur.ai/health) directly, so a dead/never-booted host pages with per-host attribution the round-robin monitors cannot give (#5933 Item 1). SINCE #7798/ADR-204 IT ALSO OWNS A PROPERTY SENTRY STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS: betteruptime_monitor.soleur_www_redirect ('soleur dot ai www redirect 301', uptime-alerts.tf) asserts that https://www.soleur.ai/ returns exactly 301 WITHOUT following it (follow_redirects = false, remember_cookies = false — the vendor rejects a 3xx expectation with either enabled, HTTP 422). Sentry's uptime checker always follows 3xx and grades the FINAL response, so its predecessor sentry_uptime_monitor.soleur_www asserted `equals 301` against the apex's 200 -- an assertion it CANNOT satisfy (structural; the measurement behind it is 10/10 most recent checks failing on 2026-09-07, not a paged-back 101-day census). That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage).

CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

description.txt: Placement, health-reschedule, and rolling deploys across the Hetzner cluster (ADR-068 Phase 4a)

Cluster of Hetzner Cloud hosts (Nomad clients, spread placement) running web app + CLI engine containers. Per-user worktrees are host-local in the ADR-068 §1 sense (they do NOT live on the shared git-data host) but they are NOT on the root NVMe — they sit on a per-host ATTACHED BLOCK VOLUME, workspacesVolume below (#6588 corrected this description, which said 'host-local NVMe' and led readers to conclude there was no volume to encrypt). At first boot a fresh host pulls the web app image from GHCR and extracts its baked bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl via docker cp (ADR-080, #5921) — a path web-1 can never take: the load-bearing reason is lifecycle{ignore_changes=[user_data]}, which means cloud-init never re-runs, so the bake reaches no live host (ADR-119 §(e)). ADR-143 (adopting, #6459) governs the return of a second web host: because cx33 was unorderable at the ADR-143 decision (2026-07-26 probe; still unorderable in hel1-dc2 on 2026-08-06, though it returned in nbg1-dc3/fsn1-dc14), web-2 returns as a fresh cattle **cpx22** (2c/4g x86, ~€19.49/mo net) — sized to web-1's MEASURED usage (~1.5 GB peak RAM / 0.48 load15 over 30d, not its over-provisioned 8g shape; ADR-143 D1) — a health-monitored standby at serving-weight 0 (NOT in the ingress rotation) until ADR-068 Phase-3 GA, since the sole-copy workspace volume lives on web-1 and a request routed to web-2 pre-flip would hit an empty workspace. TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-07-26 (ADR-143 addendum, #6966), FORCED BY STOCK: the live probe that day (/v1/datacenters .server_types.available) found the ENTIRE cx line — cx23 as well as cx33 — and the ENTIRE cax ARM line orderable in 0 of 3 EU DCs, so the earlier 'cx23, in stock in hel1' claim recorded here is FALSE and is retired. cpx22 matches cx23 on cores and RAM exactly (2c/4g) and doubles local disk, so the D1 sizing rationale is unchanged — this was a price change (+€14.00/mo), not a resize. Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. The fleet remains single-host until web-2 is provisioned by the gated web-host-create dispatch

DNS, CDN, R2 storage, zero-trust tunnel — and, from #7640/ADR-194, the HOST of the marketing/docs site, a role it did NOT carry before. A direct-upload `cloudflare_pages_project` (soleur-docs, production_branch=main, no `source` block so the Git integration is deliberately NOT used) with soleur.ai and www.soleur.ai attached as `cloudflare_pages_domain` custom domains; deploy-docs.yml publishes `_site` to it with a version-pinned `wrangler pages deploy` AFTER the same six build gates, so the gate chain stays authoritative over what is served. The point is structural, not vendor preference: Cloudflare serving the site means there is NO ORIGIN LEG and no origin certificate, which is the entire failure class the migration deletes (the apex was GitHub-Pages-hosted behind this same proxy, and GitHub refuses to issue a cert for a proxied host). Also owns the rebuilt `www -> apex` 301, as an ACCOUNT-LEVEL Bulk Redirect on the `http_request_redirect` phase with its own Free quota — NOT a rule in `cloudflare_ruleset.seo_page_redirects`, whose 10-rule Free cap and whose Rule 10 (HTTPS upgrade + its inline ACME carve-out clause) are untouched by this work. Cloudflare documents Bulk Redirects as running IN FRONT OF a Pages project, which is what lets www stay attached to the project rather than parked on a black-hole IP. No new vendor, no new bill and no DPA change: already a sub-processor, already the zone owner.

PRIVATE GHCR registry (ghcr.io/jikig-ai/soleur-web-platform + soleur-inngest-bootstrap) — the ORIGINAL host pull source, now WRITE-ONLY: still dual-pushed by CI, but DEAD AS A FALLBACK since the Phase-5 retirement — the read PAT is revoked (GET api.github.com/user -> 401) and the minter is disabled (GHCR_MINTER_DISABLED=true; pull-token mint -> 403 DENIED), verified 2026-07-30 (#7071). It receives every image and can serve none TO HOSTS. Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).

OCI-native container registry (zot) on a dedicated Hetzner host (cpx22, 2 vCPU / 4 GB, hel1, volume-backed) on the private network (10.0.1.30:5000), behind a deny-all-public firewall — the zero-touch machine-credential registry that replaces GHCR on the pull path (ADR-096, #6122). TYPE REPINNED cx23 → cpx22 on 2026-08-06 (#7309) — FORCED BY STOCK VOLATILITY, not by sizing and not by unorderability: cx23 IS orderable in hel1-dc2 as of that day's live probe, but hel1-dc2 cx23 availability changed direction twice across twelve days, the first inside 24 hours (in stock 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-25, unavailable 2026-07-26 and 2026-08-04, available again 2026-08-06 — series and sources single-sourced at zot-registry.tf, anchor 'STOCK REALITY'), and a registry type change is a destroy-then-create with no capacity reservation on the sole pull path (ADR-169), where a failed revert needs a SECOND create. cpx22 was available at all three probes. Same 2c/4g shape, so the derived arch stays amd64 and the cap stays 3072m; +€14.00/mo, operator-accepted, and not billing until the host-replace actually runs. TYPE + CAP CORRECTED 2026-08-05 (#7282): this description named a larger 4 vCPU / 8 GB server type and a hardcoded megabyte cap literal, and BOTH were stale — the file contradicted itself, correctly listing the registry's real type in its own DR-gap enumeration above. History, kept because it explains the shape: #6288 sized it cx33 in hel1 (the plan's cx32 target does not exist as a Hetzner type; cx33 is the real 8 GB type, offered in hel1 not nbg1), then #6497/#6463 REVERTED var.registry_server_type to cx23 on 2026-07-16 and the description never followed. The cap is not a literal at all — it is DERIVED as host RAM − 1024m reserve, so on the live 4 GB type it is 3072m, and the whole point of deriving it is that it cannot disagree with the host the way a hardcoded 7168m did. The cap exists so zot's ~35 GB store boot scan cannot host-OOM restart-loop the box. PINNED IMAGE — LIVE-VERIFIED as of 2026-08-12 (this description previously read CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING; that is RETRACTED 2026-08-12 (#7455) as satisfied, not as wrong-when-written): zot-registry.tf pins v2.1.20 per arch and the LIVE host now RUNS it — the registry-host-replace fired 2026-08-12T20:54:12Z (run 31639782781) and the post-replace SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK rows report zot_image_digest=95a837a0afac, which is the v2.1.20 pin's digest. The earlier blocked-on-#7278-and-#6929 clause is likewise spent: the LUKS recut fired 2026-08-10. Merging a cloud-init change is STILL inert by the OPERATOR_APPLIED_EXCLUSION contract and still needs a provisioning event — that rule is unchanged and governs the NEXT such change (#7277 closed by PR #7290; Hetzner stock struck 2026-08-06 by #7309, which repinned this host to a type available at every recorded probe — see the ADR-096 amendment). `zot_image_digest` in SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK remains the off-host answer and is what settled this: it reads 95a837a0afac on the replacement host. Keep reading it rather than the pin whenever the two could diverge again. Pulled from the PUBLIC upstream registry at boot, never from itself (the bootstrap paradox — which is also the rollback lever, since a dark zot cannot block its own replacement). FRESHNESS OWNER: no bot manages that pin (Renovate has never run against this repo — measured 2026-08-05, zero PRs, no Dependency Dashboard; its inert config was removed in #7282). Detection is a poll step on rule-audit.yml (1st + 15th) that files one idempotent issue; enforcement is zot-image-staleness.test.sh in infra-validation; the analysis of record is zot-image.provenance.md. Before #7282 the only mechanism was a prose comment telling a human to run crane digest, and the pin sat 18 releases behind for ~18 months. The 60 GB store volume re-fills ONLY from a fresh CI dual-push — NOT from GHCR. Its previous description as a 'disposable GHCR mirror' with an 'atomic GHCR fallback' is RETRACTED 2026-07-30 (#7071): the sibling ghcr node in this same enumeration is now marked DEAD AS A FALLBACK (read PAT revoked -> 401, minter disabled -> 403 DENIED), so an emptied store leaves NO registry any host can pull from until CI re-pushes. The blobs stay reproducible, so this is a recoverability property, never a free one — every recut/replace of this volume takes production's only pull path offline for the gap. Hosts pull the SAME @sha256 digests here (crane-copy from CI preserves them); cosign verifies the zot-stored .sig offline against the unchanged pinned root. Plain-HTTP on the private net (integrity via cosign digest-pinning, not TLS). AT REST: guest-side LUKS, CODE-DECLARED / LIVE-PENDING (`hcloud_volume.registry` is declared RAW — no `format` — and cloud-init-registry.yml luksFormats/luksOpens it as /dev/mapper/registry, keyed by random_password.registry_luks via doppler_secret.registry_luks_key). The LIVE device is still plaintext ext4 until the guarded `registry-luks-recut` workflow_dispatch is fired; that vehicle shipped UNFIRED (#6929), so this is a code-declared posture, NOT a live-verified one. Low sensitivity (our own OCI blobs + cosign signatures, no user/repo data); integrity comes from cosign digest-pinning, not at-rest encryption (encryption-posture-ledger.json) The 60 GB store volume re-fills EITHER from a fresh CI dual-push OR, since #7277/ADR-169, from a CI-mediated GHCR restore (scripts/registry-restore-from-ghcr.sh, chained automatically after registry-luks-recut). Its earlier wording denying any GHCR refill path is RETRACTED 2026-08-05 (the literal phrase is not repeated here: AC18 is a whole-file count, and quoting it would false-fail a corrected model). Note the restore is CI-mediated and carries the REQUIRED pin set only — it is not a mirror and not a host-reachable fallback, and its authorization condition is ADR-169's rehearsed-restore gate.

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.

description.txt: Every user's checked-out repository. SOLE-COPY: refs/checkpoints/* is pushed by no refspec, session-sync.ts autocommits only knowledge-base/**, and signup-provisioned workspaces have no git remote at all — so ADR-068 §1's 'GitHub remains the durable rehydration source' does NOT hold here and there is no durable second copy anywhere (no upstream to rehydrate from). ENCRYPTED AT REST as of the 2026-07-23 cutover — the gap #6588/ADR-119 opened (PLAINTEXT ext4 while the published privacy policy claimed LUKS) is closed. HISTORY: an earlier 2026-07-20 cutover attempt (run 29782780158) landed /mnt/data on crypto_LUKS for ~27 minutes before its own dead-man timer silently remounted the retained plaintext volume over it (#6812) — do not cite that landing as the current state. The 2026-07-23 cutover is the one that certified: `workspaces-luks-verify` run **30040444418** reported `SOLEUR_WORKSPACES_READYZ ready=true writable=true populated=true workspace_count=8 expected=8` against `/dev/mapper/workspaces` — a mechanically measured verdict, not an assumed one (this distinction, per ADR-140, is the whole feature). web-2's instance was knowingly left plaintext (never served, empty) until its 2026-07-17 teardown (#6538/#6463). The fleet is single-host as of this writing, so no plaintext member remains — but that is a statement about the CURRENT fleet, NOT an invariant: the fresh web-2 (repinned cpx22, #6966) is born with its own per-host workspaces volume (hcloud_volume.workspaces, web-2 key) as RAW/empty PLAINTEXT, because the guest-side LUKS path for a FRESH host is the deferred #6931 work (ADR-141 D3) and the workspaces_luks attachment is web-1-bound and outside the birth fan-out (#6964). That member holds NO user data (sole copy is web-1's volume; web-2 is never routed pre-flip, dns.tf app record is web-1-only and the #6575 anti-pooling gate fail-closes), and it MUST NOT take serving weight while plaintext — re-evaluate at the ADR-068 Phase-3 GA flip

nodes.title: Shared git-data

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). NOT YET PROVISIONED (#6977): this element is DECLARED in IaC and the host has never existed — an authenticated `terraform state list` returns zero git-data members — so every behaviour described here is the TARGET state, not the live one. It remains unborn until the gated `git-data-host-create` dispatch runs. The birth-readiness interlock that held that route is RELEASED by #6982, which ships the off-host emitter (ADR-149 item 1): the host now emits boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal the birth job POLLS, and gc faults to Better Stack — so a green apply and a dark host are no longer indistinguishable. What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), shipped unfired because a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. CORRECTED 2026-08-03 (#7204): the route is NO LONGER unfired — it has been dispatched FOUR times (one dry-run success 2026-07-30, then three real-host failures) and has consumed three paid cpx22 hosts IN THE SEPARATE #7025 REHEARSAL TERRAFORM ROOT — which is why 'the host has never existed' above stays true: no rehearsal host is ever created at the hcloud_server.git_data address. The most recent, run 30649892865, died at `stage:luks_open` with mount(2) returning ESRCH: the birth `mkfs.ext4 -O quota,project` set the ext4 quota feature, whose mount forces `ext4_enable_quotas()` and a `quota_v2` module the 24.04 cloud image does not ship (linux-modules-extra absent). That is the CURRENT birth-blocking fact, fixed by #7204 (ADR-159) but NOT yet re-rehearsed — the evidence file is still absent, so the gate still refuses. The runbook banner is a FURTHER hold, not the only one. AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). Ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897), pending cutover

Source control, CI/CD, issue tracking, and releases. ALSO, THROUGH the #7640 cutover (COMPLETED 2026-09-03), the HOST of the marketing/docs site and its certificate-admin plane: GitHub Pages SERVED soleur.ai + www.soleur.ai, and `PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` (custom-domain set/clear) plus `GET .../pages/health` WERE the endpoints cron-gh-pages-cert-reissue drove inside a DNS-only window (ADR-125) — that routine is now DISARMED, so read this clause as describing the rollback-path mechanism, not a live one. That hosting role ENDED at the cutover (ADR-194, #7640, applied 2026-09-03): the same Eleventy build is published to Cloudflare Pages and apex+www DNS was repointed, after which the GitHub Pages configuration is RETAINED BUT DNS-DETACHED AND NO LONGER REPUBLISHED. Retained deliberately — it is the rollback target — and NOT because it still serves. NOTE THE NARROWING (PR5, AC56): while the publish leg still ran, a DNS-only revert WAS the whole rollback; since PR5 retired that leg the retained content is FROZEN at the last PR4-era build, so restoring this origin now takes THREE acts (re-add the publish leg, redeploy, revert DNS) rather than one — and FOUR whenever apex-origin-probe.sh still reports SERVING-FROM-CLOUDFLARE-PAGES after the DNS revert, because the custom-domain ATTACHMENT can route independently of the record and must be reverted too (cutover runbook, `### Procedure` step 3). Do not quote the bare count without that conditional. Read the cert-admin path as DEAD ON THE LIVE SITE from that moment, in the same sense the `ghcr` node is dead on the pull path: the endpoints still answer, but eligibility requires the hostname to resolve to GitHub anycast and it no longer does, so no certificate can ever issue again and the origin cert stays expired by construction. This is why the reissue routine is DISARMED (apex-topology precondition + the daily detector cron removed) rather than left armed: post-cutover it would flip `www` to proxied=false and structurally could not restore it. Deletion of the GitHub Pages hosting config, its CNAME file and the remediation subsystem is DEFERRED, not done — see ADR-194 Addendum 2026-08-20 §2.
