It receives every image and can serve none TO HOSTS. Scope that precisely: since #7277 it demonstrably serves CI, which reads it under packages: read to re-materialise the zot store (ADR-169). The dead edge is host->GHCR, not GHCR itself. This is STRUCTURAL, not a lapsed chore: App installation tokens authenticate docker login but are DENIED docker pull on private repo-linked packages (ADR-088 arm-b), so no zero-touch GHCR pull credential can exist FOR A HOST — only a personal one. This is scoped to App installation tokens on hosts and must not be read as absolute: a CI job's GITHUB_TOKEN in this repo's context is a different credential class, and it is what ADR-169's restore path uses. Consequence: zot is the SOLE pull path and the CI zot mirror is now release-blocking (ADR-096 amendment 2026-07-30). Still bakes the host bootstrap scripts + hooks.json.tmpl, extracted via docker cp at first boot to keep cloud-init user_data under Hetzner's 32,768-byte cap (ADR-080, #5921).

External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage).

So the AT-REST claim above is unchanged and the ledger keeps its exception — what changed is that the mechanism is built rather than absent

nodes.title: Cloudflare Tunnel

description.txt: Zero-trust inbound access — no exposed ports. ONE tunnel (tunnel.tf) with THREE ingress rules (deploy./ssh./registry.). DETERMINISM IS NOW STRUCTURAL, not one-connector: since #6594/PR-A all three ingress services are ORIGIN-RELATIVE (deploy. → http://10.0.1.10:9000, ssh. → ssh://10.0.1.10:22, registry. → tcp://10.0.1.30:5000), so whichever connector replica CF selects proxies to the correct origin (ADR-114 I2 discharged for all three). This — not 'localhost: means this host' — is what makes the management plane deterministic. NOT AN INVARIANT: the earlier 'exactly ONE connector, ADR-114 I1 enforced #6425' claim is FALSE in production. The server.tf web_tunnel_connector gate lives at cloud-init create-time user_data only, and hcloud_server.web carries ignore_changes=[user_data], so it never re-runs on a booted host. (Historical: web-2 booted 2026-07-13 BEFORE the gate merged 2026-07-15, so TWO connectors were live and measured; web-2 was retired 2026-07-17 (#6538/#6463) and var.web_hosts is now single-host.) I1 is a construction-time gate presented as a runtime precondition — it governs only future fresh hosts, and that stays true after #6441: the NIC gate added there is FIRST-BOOT (runcmd is once-per-instance), so a fresh connector host now waits for its private address before registering and DEFERS rather than aborting on timeout, but no gate re-runs on a host that is already up. CF binds ingress to a TUNNEL and picks a connector per edge colo; before the origin-relative pin a SECOND connector silently made every non-fan-out route (deploy-status, inngest-liveness, infra-config WRITEs, ssh.) answer from whichever replica the caller's colo selected — #6425 (16h of false inngest-down alarms), #6594 (a false-green infra-config apply), #6416. Origin-relative ingress makes that harmless: the coin flip no longer determines correctness. Standing guard: the */15 connector census in scheduled-inngest-health.yml (vantage-independent; a response-poll is colo-sticky and proves nothing). Management plane only: app.soleur.ai does NOT traverse the tunnel (direct CF-proxied A record, dns.tf); no cloudflared on zot/git-data/inngest (ADR-096).

Read .server_types.available, never .supported (the hcloud CLI has the same trap). A fresh cpx22 CAN take the docker-cp bake path (unlike the frozen web-1). NOTE the DR gap the same probe exposes: web-1 (cx33), soleur-grok-dogfood (cx33) and soleur-registry (then cx23, repinned to cpx22 by #7309) all ran on types that were unorderable ON THAT DATE — restated 2026-08-06, when a live probe found both cx23 and cx33 AVAILABLE again in hel1-dc2, so the gap is not that these types are gone but that availability is not a property of the type and flips in either direction; each rebuild is a type decision even when the probe is green — they run fine but NONE can be COUNTED ON to rebuild on its current type (#6460) — the two cx33 hosts because cx33 is not orderable in hel1 where they run, and the registry (now cpx22) because a green probe is a moment, not a reservation. The fleet remains single-host until web-2 is provisioned by the gated web-host-create dispatch

nodes.title: Shared git-data

description.txt: Shared bare git repos (objects/refs) over the private net; per-user worktrees stay host-local on NVMe. The git-data host holds the per-ref monotonic max generation and writer-side-CAS-rejects stale lease writes (ADR-068). NOT YET PROVISIONED (#6977): this element is DECLARED in IaC and the host has never existed — an authenticated `terraform state list` returns zero git-data members — so every behaviour described here is the TARGET state, not the live one. It remains unborn until the gated `git-data-host-create` dispatch runs. The birth-readiness interlock that held that route is RELEASED by #6982, which ships the off-host emitter (ADR-149 item 1): the host now emits boot-stage fatals to Sentry from a baked DSN, a `stage:boot_complete` signal the birth job POLLS, and gc faults to Better Stack — so a green apply and a dark host are no longer indistinguishable. What holds the route now is MECHANICAL, not prose: `git_data_rung2_rehearsal_gate` (#6982 A3) runs in the same dispatch job before any provider is contacted and refuses unless `git-data-rung2-boot-evidence.env` attests a rung-2 boot rehearsal hash-bound to the CURRENT template — a hash-of-hashes over the cloud-init plus every `file()`-bound payload, so the evidence self-invalidates on any later edit to what ships. That file is absent, so a dispatch exits 1. #7025 shipped the gated rehearsal ROUTE that produces it (a separate Terraform root + `workflow_dispatch`), shipped unfired because a PR merges atomically, so evidence committed alongside its own harness would attest a rehearsal that never ran. CORRECTED 2026-08-03 (#7204): the route is NO LONGER unfired — it has been dispatched FOUR times (one dry-run success 2026-07-30, then three real-host failures) and has consumed three paid cpx22 hosts IN THE SEPARATE #7025 REHEARSAL TERRAFORM ROOT — which is why 'the host has never existed' above stays true: no rehearsal host is ever created at the hcloud_server.git_data address. The most recent, run 30649892865, died at `stage:luks_open` with mount(2) returning ESRCH: the birth `mkfs.ext4 -O quota,project` set the ext4 quota feature, whose mount forces `ext4_enable_quotas()` and a `quota_v2` module the 24.04 cloud image does not ship (linux-modules-extra absent). That is the CURRENT birth-blocking fact, fixed by #7204 (ADR-159) but NOT yet re-rehearsed — the evidence file is still absent, so the gate still refuses. The runbook banner is a FURTHER hold, not the only one. AT REST: the target store is PLAINTEXT ext4 (`hcloud_volume.git_data`, `format = "ext4"`, no LUKS apparatus) — a fresh `hcloud_volume.git_data_luks` cutover target is declared alongside it (git-data-luks.tf) but is not the live store (`GIT_DATA_STORE_ENABLED` gates the cutover). Ledgered exception (encryption-posture-ledger.json, tracking #6897), pending cutover

nodes.technology: Bare git repos over private net

description.txt: External uptime/heartbeat monitoring (BetterStackHQ/better-uptime) AND a Logs warehouse that CI both POLLS and — since #7278/ADR-172 — WRITES TO. TWO Logs sources as of #7772, not one: 2457081 (soleur-inngest-vector-prd, eu-fsn-3) is the SHARED source the web hosts, the Inngest node and the zot registry all multiplex into with host_name as the sole discriminator; 2734275 (soleur-git-data-prd, platform http, eu-central-1a, table soleur_git_data_prd, 90d retention) belongs to git-data ALONE. The split exists because git-data is the lowest-trust host in the fleet — its `git` account serves every connected user's push — and baking the SHARED credential there meant a git-data compromise forced a rotation that darkened the web host's shipper and the registry's and cost two host replaces. Do NOT re-point local.betterstack_logs_ingest_url at the new source: that local serves the four NON-git-data consumers and moving it would put the web hosts and the registry on git-data's stream. The 'CI polls read-only' clause this description carried until 2026-08-06 is FALSE and was corrected, not softened: registry-zot-inventory.yml POSTs a SOLEUR_ZOT_INVENTORY line to the Logs INGEST endpoint using BETTERSTACK_LOGS_TOKEN read from soleur/prd, and no GitHub Actions workflow had ever POSTed here before. A CI POST bypasses Vector's VRL scrub (MOST host emitters reach this source through a Vector agent that redacts; a runner curl does not — and since #7440/ADR-184 neither does the registry host's zot-log shipper, which runs no Vector and owns its own redaction, so 'every host emitter is Vector-scrubbed' is no longer true and must not be relied on as a PII-safety inference; and in the other direction, the user-serving application container's pino WARN+ stream IS Vector-transited but its `userIdHash` is pseudonymised in the APPLICATION before egress rather than by Vector's HMAC stage, which short-circuits when the payload carries no raw userId -- so 'Vector-scrubbed' also does not mean 'Vector is what pseudonymised it', and that stream is the highest-sensitivity payload on source 2457081), so a CI-emitted marker must be PII-free BY CONSTRUCTION and is asserted so by a field allow-list test. The read direction is unchanged and is still the ONLY thing that grades a CI-emitted marker: the emitter's exit code is not evidence, so a run is green only after it reads its own run_id back out through the ClickHouse path (ADR-172 §2). Apex + inngest + registry-disk heartbeats, plus (#6438/#6548) TWO new per-host web heartbeats — web_zot_consumer (the zot-consumer serviceability probe, #6438 §1) and web_nic_guard (the §3 private-NIC-guard liveness beat, #6438 §3), both for_each var.web_hosts — and git-data, whose git_data_prd beat is FED by the web-host consumer probe (#6548) but is **deliberately NOT armed** — #6982 (D-HB) withdrew the plan to arm it, and #6548 alone now owns the decision. Three reasons, any one disqualifying: the `arm_one` call for it lives in the PER-MERGE apply job, so creating the heartbeat would make an unborn flag-off host's health a merge-blocking dependency for the whole repository; a TCP connect-and-close to :22 proves the port is OPEN, not that git transport SERVES, and sshd is up before runcmd runs — so a host whose LUKS never mounted answers on :22 and beats GREEN, installing a green light over the exact failure the interlock exists to catch; and the object pool may be at 10/10. git-data's boot correctness is instead reported HOST-SIDE by its own emitter (#6982). Registry-liveness remains paused until #6537's feeder ships and a beat is measured. All three new/newly-fed web beats (web_zot_consumer, web_nic_guard, git_data_prd) are arm-gated by the automated measure-then-arm PATCH in apply-web-platform-infra.yml (ADR-117 amendment #6438). ALSO a per-host origin absence detector that probes each web host's CF-proxied hostname (web-N.app.soleur.ai/health) directly, so a dead/never-booted host pages with per-host attribution the round-robin monitors cannot give (#5933 Item 1). SINCE #7798/ADR-204 IT ALSO OWNS A PROPERTY SENTRY STRUCTURALLY CANNOT EXPRESS: betteruptime_monitor.soleur_www_redirect ('soleur dot ai www redirect 301', uptime-alerts.tf) asserts that https://www.soleur.ai/ returns exactly 301 WITHOUT following it (follow_redirects = false, remember_cookies = false — the vendor rejects a 3xx expectation with either enabled, HTTP 422). Sentry's uptime checker always follows 3xx and grades the FINAL response, so its predecessor sentry_uptime_monitor.soleur_www asserted `equals 301` against the apex's 200 -- an assertion it CANNOT satisfy (structural; the measurement behind it is 10/10 most recent checks failing on 2026-09-07, not a paged-back 101-day census). That monitor is now soleur_www_reachability asserting 2xx. Read the consequence rather than inferring it from the apex pattern: redirect-health is SINGLE-VENDOR. Apex reachability is deliberately second-sourced across Sentry and Better Stack, but the www 301 is watched here ALONE, because no other vendor in the stack can see the pre-redirect hop. A Better Stack outage leaves it uncovered. Detection is 180s cadence plus a 1200s confirmation window, i.e. 1380s ~23 min worst case (the cadence term is additive), which is also the real bound behind dns.tf's Camp B 'one monitor interval' acceptance — a bound that was UNBOUNDED before this, the assertion behind it having never once passed. The Logs source receives SOLEUR_ZOT_DISK + SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC self-reports from the deny-all registry host AND SOLEUR_PRIVATE_NIC from web-1 (the §3 web-host guard, detect+emit+alarm, NO reboot — ADR-123) and is polled from GitHub Actions via betterstack-query.sh for the zot restart-loop recurrence alarm (#6291) + follow-through soak probes — log-content recurrence alarms are in-repo GH-cron pollers, not native Better Stack alerts (ADR-096) — with ONE exception since #8097/ADR-218: Logs alerts for pure stateless per-bucket counts are Terraform-managed via BetterStackHQ/logtail, and the first, soleur-monitor-send-failed-prd, pages when a web-1 monitor unit's own Resend/Sentry send fails (the signal whose detector must survive a Sentry outage).

Error tracking + alerting, Sentry-as-IaC (ADR-031; apps/web-platform/infra/sentry/, auto-applied on push to main by apply-sentry-infra.yml — its `paths:` filter is the whole `infra/sentry/**` tree and the plan is FULL-ROOT since #6589, so declaring a resource applies it and DELETING one really destroys it, gated pre-merge by `sentry-destroy-required` + `[ack-destroy]`. The filter was widened from a 3-file list because the retired `-target=` allowlist had doubled as the gate for declared-but-never-applied). Org `jikigai-eu` on the EU/DE cluster. TWO distinct hostname classes: the Terraform/dashboard API is the ORG SUBDOMAIN (`https://<org>.sentry.io/api/`, see main.tf's provider block — NOT `eu.sentry.io`, whose regional host rewrites `-eu`-suffixed slugs to the literal `eu` org via an activeorg-cookie hijack, 302→401, breaking every read/write); DSN ingest is `de.sentry.io` (DE residency, Art. 30 PA8 §(e)). Holds the LARGER of the two paging surfaces: the issue alerts (issue-alerts.tf), the cron monitors (cron-monitors.tf — one per scheduled workflow, `failure_issue_threshold` opens an issue on a missed check-in) and the uptime monitors (uptime-monitors.tf). It is a no-SSH paging path — a host that never finished booting still pages through here. It is deliberately NOT the only one: `betterstack` is a SECOND-SOURCE vendor that pages independently precisely so a Sentry outage is survivable (see its own edge to founder). Do not 'consolidate' the two — the redundancy is the design.
